title: Efficient Equivalence Checking of Nonlinear Analog Circuits using Gradient Ascent
problem: Efficiently verifying that two nonlinear analog circuit designs are functionally equivalent by identifying critical regions where their behaviors diverge. Key challenges include mapping both designs to a common state space, computing gradients through nonlinear systems, and excluding unreachable state space regions.
motivation: Equivalence checking is critical for verifying circuit correctness and preventing costly design errors before manufacturing.
method: The approach uses gradient ascent—an algorithm that climbs toward better solutions—to search through the space of states both analog circuits can occupy. It handles nonlinear behavior by using local linear approximations and Kronecker Canonical Form, a mathematical transformation that puts both circuit designs into a standard comparable format. A custom-designed scoring function guides the search toward regions where the circuits differ most, while geometric filtering techniques eliminate impossible states the circuits could never physically reach.
key_novelty: The key advance combines gradient-ascent search with Kronecker Canonical Form—a transformation that standardizes state spaces—to efficiently find where nonlinear analog circuits diverge.
contributions: Gradient-ascent methodology for efficient nonlinear analog circuit equivalence checking
KCF-based canonical state space mapping technique for circuit design alignment
Vector projection approach for excluding unreachable state space regions
Up to 468x speedup compared to conventional equivalence checking methods
